reviewContext.userProblem: implementation-wave-outcome routes every fully blocked wave (implementation_blocked && !partial_success) to the terminal implementation-blocked-output step. In monja security batch 1 (sessions 630-651), almost all such blockers were scope or contract gaps the plan owner could decide: a file outside writePaths, a missing additive port/projection field, an unspecified authority/readback rule, or an unowned fixture/composition file. Each gap forced an operator to hand-write a plan amendment, patch the dispatch manifest and restart from plan-checkpoint (6 consecutive restarts for one unit).
requiredOutcomes: A fully blocked wave whose blockers are all scope/contract gaps routes to step4-impl-plan-create with a bounded checkpointAmendment (reason blocked-wave-scope-or-contract). Ineligible or budget-exhausted waves still end in implementation-blocked-output. Partial-success routing to reconcile-implementations is unchanged.
The amendment budget is bounded and shared across dispatch and blocked-wave amendments (MAX_CHECKPOINT_AMENDMENTS = 2, imported from dispatch-wave.py) and documented.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: D1: rule-based eligibility in implementation-wave-outcome.py (wave shape blocked/pending only, blockerType implementation-dependency only, no environment flag, every substantive blocker carries a path/dependency/scope resume signal, fail-closed denylist over all scanned fields including resumeCriteria lists, resolvable checkpoint, amendment <= 16384 bytes).
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Deterministic and conservative; a false negative only falls back to today's blocked output, which is safe.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: D2: amendmentRound = first-parent checkpoint commits from manifest originalHead to HEAD minus 1; MAX_CHECKPOINT_AMENDMENTS stays 2 and is imported from dispatch-wave.py.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: The join inbox has no checkpoint messages, so Git is the only shared evidence; every amendment from either source creates exactly one checkpoint commit, so one count bounds both. Existing tests and docs pin 2 (user-qa Q1).

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: D3/D4: payload and when gain amendment_required (required) and optional checkpointAmendment; workflow transitions become step4-impl-plan-create, implementation-blocked-output, reconcile-implementations with mutually exclusive labels.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Reuses the existing checkpointAmendment shape and Step 4 -> Step 5 -> plan-checkpoint -> redispatch path without adding steps.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: D5: wave-summary.json records amendmentDecision with up to 10 ineligibleReasons; implementation-blocked-output.md is unchanged.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Gives operators a deterministic reason a blocked wave was not auto-amended.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: D6: step4/step5/plan-checkpoint prompt rules for blocked-wave-scope-or-contract (exact writePaths, additive contracts, single owner per file, dated amendment section, no redesign, originalHead preserved, dated designDecisionsAndRationale manifest entry, blocked implementation changes unstaged).
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Keeps the shared bound working (originalHead never rewritten) and guarantees the amendment checkpoint contains exactly one changed manifest.

designDecisionsAndRationale.decision: D7: mock-scenario-blocked-wave-amendment.json uses per-node response arrays (blocked wave -> amendment -> redispatch -> success); escalation instead of substitution if riela rejects arrays.
designDecisionsAndRationale.rationale: Array sequencing with last-entry repeat is confirmed by check-package-compat.ts:241-255 and existing fixtures (user-qa Q2).

intentionalTradeoffs: The bound stays 2 total per run instead of being raised; a blocked-wave amendment resolves every blocker of the wave at once.
A resumed run whose manifest originalHead predates the run counts earlier checkpoints too, which is stricter than dispatch's per-session inbox count.
Conservative eligibility markers may exclude some real scope gaps; those waves fall back to today's blocked output.
Mock scenarios do not execute command scripts, so the eligibility logic is covered by unit tests against temp git repos.
supportedEdgeCases: Eligible fully blocked wave at round 0 and round 1 (shared counter after one dispatch amendment).
Budget exhaustion at round 2 -> implementation-blocked-output with an amendment-budget-exhausted reason.

Ineligible gate types, environment flags, each denylist family (including markers only in blocker or plan-level resumeCriteria), non-string resumeCriteria entries, string-only blockers, marker-only plans.
Non-git or unresolvable checkpoint lineage (ineligible, never an exception).
Oversize amendment (> 16384 bytes) -> ineligible with amendment-oversize, no raise.
Partial-success waves with eligible-looking blockers keep the reconcile route.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: TMPDIR located inside a git repository (non-git temp-root ineligibility check assumes it is not).
